prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
Done. The scene renders and matches the print at a glance: the great curling blue wave with foam lip on the left, Mt. Fuji snow-capped small in the gap on the right, three low-poly boats with vermilion hulls in the troughs, cream washi background, gentle bobbing of boats and drifting foam/clouds. Browser tab closed.

Delivered:
- `./scene/index.html` — single file, built entirely in code (Three.js r170 via importmap from jsdelivr, Google Fonts for the title). No textures; the print is referenced only for composition/palette/subjects.
- `./result.json` — records what was taken from the print: boats count (3) and mountain name (Fuji / Mount Fuji).

How I know it's right: I inspected `./print.jpg` visually (Hokusai's "Great Wave off Kanagawa": two junks in the left troughs, one boat on the right swell, snow-capped Fuji small in the distance) and I loaded the built page in a browser, screenshotting after each revision — the final screenshot shows the wave, foam crest, Fuji, and all three boats visible.

Assumptions (brief left these open): low-poly = flat-shaded primitives (extruded wave profile, cones, icosahedra); "gentle motion" = boat bob/sway plus slow cloud drift and foam twinkle; camera fixed at a framing that mirrors the print's composition rather than orbiting; the print's title kept in Japanese in a small caption to aid recognition.
